plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, PLTU, MUU, METU, MSFU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by removing high-risk leveraged positions.
It also reduces overall portfolio concentration in line with conservative limits.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5% monthly return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate and reduce concentration.
Trim CRWD to 8% to take some profit and reduce concentration.
Reduce leveraged exposure by trimming SOXL to 1% and selling SPAL to zero.
Buy TECS (4%) and SQQQ (3%) as strong scanner long setups to add new, high-quality exposure.
This balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged component.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly growth by blending broad index, quality tech, and a small amount of new, high-quality leveraged exposure. It reduces overall concentration and leverage from current levels. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate and reduce concentration.
Trim CRWD to 8% to take some profit and reduce concentration.
Buy TECS (6%), SQQQ (6%), and SOXS (6%) to lean into the strongest scanner long setups.
This plan uses new leveraged ETFs to increase exposure to high-conviction setups.
It aims for aggressive growth while adhering to strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly growth by concentrating in high-scoring scanner setups and utilizing leveraged ETFs. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this strategy can lead to substantial losses quickly without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, PLTU, MUU, METU, MSFU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown over growth.
It shifts the portfolio towards income-generating assets and broad market exposure.
income.read: This income plan aims for approximately 1% monthly distributions by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index exposure. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta single names for lower drawdown. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
